health:
health
  usage:  health
  does:   Read the gateway's health report.
  output: api version, aggregate state, queue depth, worker count, image digest, and one line per service
  note:   The gateway is the only health authority.
  note:   A degraded service keeps the stack reachable; a down service does not.
dataset list:
dataset list
  usage:  dataset list
  does:   List the datasets in the active profile.
  output: one line per dataset: data_version, name, candles, first_bar, last_bar, bytes
  note:   Rows are sorted by data_version.
dataset show:
dataset show
  usage:  dataset show <data_version>
  does:   Read one dataset record, including its stored object identity.
  output: data_version, name, coverage, bytes, object_key, sha256, quality, created_at
  note:   A tolerant upload also prints its quality report and skipped rows.
dataset upload:
dataset upload
  usage:  dataset upload <csv-path> [--name <name>] [--tolerant]
  does:   Upload one CSV and print the record the gateway created or reused.
  output: the dataset record, with data_version, coverage, and quality
  note:   The file body is the request; the gateway owns the limit and the hash.
  note:   --tolerant uses the tolerant ingest and prints the quality report.
  note:   An identical upload returns the existing record.
config list:
config list
  usage:  config list
  does:   List the run configurations in the active profile.
  output: one line per config: config_id, name, origin, validity, hash
  note:   The list merges the read-only repository mount with uploaded configs.
config show:
config show
  usage:  config show <config_id>
  does:   Read one configuration summary and its validation state.
  output: config_id, name, origin, valid, message, config_hash
  note:   An invalid config prints its parser message and no hash.
run submit:
run submit
  usage:  run submit <data_version> <config_id> [--model-artifact <id>]
  does:   Submit a run and print its id and initial state.
  output: run_id, status, created
  note:   The gateway validates the dataset and config before accepting the run.
  note:   `--model-artifact` reuses a frozen model stage artifact; strategy, execution, and portfolio are recomputed.
  note:   A duplicate submission returns the existing run with created=false.
run status:
run status
  usage:  run status <run_id>
  does:   Read one run's stages, provenance, artifacts, and digest.
  output: run identity, optional frozen model artifact reference, stage lines, artifact lines, canonical digest, error
  note:   A failed run prints its error line and no digest.
run list:
run list
  usage:  run list [--status <state>] [--limit <n>]
  does:   List runs in the active profile.
  output: one line per run: run_id, status, config, data_version, submitted_at, elapsed
  note:   --status accepts queued, running, succeeded, failed, or cancelled.
run fetch:
run fetch
  usage:  run fetch <run_id> <directory>
  does:   Download every artifact of a run into a local directory.
  output: the run id, the target directory, and one line per artifact
  note:   The artifact name is relative to the bundle root; a traversal name is refused.
  note:   The directory is created when it does not exist.
run cancel:
run cancel
  usage:  run cancel <run_id>
  does:   Cancel a queued or running run and print its new state.
  output: the run detail after the transition
  note:   Cancelling a terminal run is refused with run.conflict.
stage run model:
stage run model
  usage:  stage run model <data_version> <config_id>
  does:   Submit a diagnostic model stage run.
  output: stage_run_id, state, created
  note:   The model artifact is diagnostic: it is never evidence and has no canonical digest.
  note:   A duplicate submission returns the existing stage with created=false.
stage run strategy:
stage run strategy
  usage:  stage run strategy <model_artifact_id> <config_id>
  does:   Submit a diagnostic strategy stage over a frozen model artifact.
  output: stage_run_id, state, created
  note:   The strategy simulates its own position; the coupled run supplies the position execution actually holds.
  note:   A standalone decision sequence can differ from the coupled run because it has no execution feedback.
  note:   The decisions bundle is diagnostic and carries no fills, cash, P&L, or canonical digest.
stage run portfolio:
stage run portfolio
  usage:  stage run portfolio <decisions_artifact_id> <config_id>
  does:   Submit a diagnostic portfolio stage over a frozen decisions artifact.
  output: stage_run_id, state, created
  note:   The stage replays execution fills through portfolio accounting; it does not decide a signal.
  note:   The execution and portfolio bundles are diagnostic and carry no canonical digest.
  note:   The stage artifact is never a backtest input or a baseline.
  note:   `stage show` lists the artifacts; use `stage fetch` to read portfolio/metrics.json and its exposure.
stage explain:
stage explain
  usage:  stage explain <stage_run_id> --bar <n>
  does:   Read one published strategy decision record.
  output: decision, side, reason, position before/after, and the published evidence fields
  note:   The shell selects the record with matching bar_index; it never recomputes the decision.
  note:   --json prints the selected decision record.
stage list:
stage list
  usage:  stage list [--kind model|strategy|portfolio] [--status <state>] [--limit <n>]
  does:   List diagnostic stage runs in the active profile.
  output: one line per stage: stage_run_id, kind, state, config, submitted_at, artifact
  note:   Rows are newest first, then by stage_run_id.
stage show:
stage show
  usage:  stage show <stage_run_id>
  does:   Read one diagnostic stage run and its artifact files.
  output: identity, state, owner, config, input, provenance, attempts, error, artifact files
  note:   A stage detail always carries evidence=false.
stage events:
stage events
  usage:  stage events <stage_run_id> --timeframe <tf>
  does:   Read the model event batch for one timeframe.
  output: the event table for the timeframe and one coverage line per report timeframe
  note:   The shell reads events.csv and report.json; it computes no model value.
  note:   --json prints one deterministic JSON value.
stage fetch:
stage fetch
  usage:  stage fetch <stage_run_id> <directory>
  does:   Download every artifact of a stage into a local directory.
  output: the stage id, the target directory, and one line per artifact
  note:   Every artifact is checked against its recorded size and SHA-256.
  note:   A traversal name is refused.
stage cancel:
stage cancel
  usage:  stage cancel <stage_run_id>
  does:   Cancel a queued or running stage and print its new state.
  output: the stage detail after the transition
  note:   Cancelling a terminal stage is refused with stage.conflict.
stage delete:
stage delete
  usage:  stage delete <stage_run_id>
  does:   Delete one diagnostic stage run and its artifact objects.
  output: the deleted stage_run_id
  note:   A run and a research record are never touched.
research create:
research create
  usage:  research create --tier <model|strategy|portfolio> --hypothesis <text> --partition <name> --data-version <digest> --config <config_id> [--criteria <criteria_id>] --green-criteria <json> --code-commit <commit> [--baseline <id>] [--seed <n>] [--analytics <true|false>]
  does:   Create one v3 improvement-run pre-registration.
  output: improvement_id, tier, state, manifest fields, and timestamps
  note:   The server assigns the improvement_id and created_utc; the manifest is immutable.
  note:   A repeated public create is a new pre-registration; an internal same-id create is idempotent.
  note:   An improvement run is a coupled pipeline run: the config must carry a strategy, and model tier still runs strategy and portfolio.
  note:   --criteria is required for a strategy or portfolio run; it is optional for model.
research submit:
research submit
  usage:  research submit <improvement_id>
  does:   Submit the coupled pipeline run for a created pre-registration.
  output: the improvement detail with pipeline_run_id and state=submitted
  note:   A duplicate submit is refused with research.conflict.
  note:   The canonical digest is linked when the run produces it, not at submission.
research list:
research list
  usage:  research list [--tier <tier>] [--state <state>] [--limit <n>]
  does:   List improvement runs in the active profile.
  output: one line per run: improvement_id, tier, state, decision, created_at, submitted_at, decided_at
  note:   Rows are newest first.
research show:
research show
  usage:  research show <improvement_id>
  does:   Read one improvement run and lazily link a successful digest.
  output: state, decision, note, manifest, pipeline run, canonical digest, and timestamps
  note:   A failed run remains submitted with no digest.
research compare:
research compare
  usage:  research compare <improvement_id> [--baseline <id>]
  does:   Compare the candidate's published numbers with a baseline.
  output: candidate and baseline ids and digests, metric rows, and an unavailability note
  note:   The comparison reads model/report.json coverage or portfolio/metrics.json; it never recomputes a model or metric.
  note:   A historical baseline row with no pipeline run has null baseline values.
research decide:
research decide
  usage:  research decide <improvement_id> --decision <accepted|rejected|no-edge|invalidated|new-hypothesis> --note <text>
  does:   Record exactly one human decision and its registry row.
  output: the decided improvement detail
  note:   A non-empty note is required; an accepted decision also requires a succeeded run and canonical digest.
  note:   A second decision is refused with research.conflict.
  note:   An accepted decision appends one baseline; an invalidated decision appends one tombstone.
baseline list:
baseline list
  usage:  baseline list
  does:   List accepted baselines in the active profile.
  output: one line per baseline: baseline_id, tier, run_id, improvement_id, accepted_by, accepted_on, scope, supersedes
  note:   Historical baseline rows are retained; no row is deleted.
baseline show:
baseline show
  usage:  baseline show <model|strategy|portfolio>
  does:   Show the current accepted baseline for one tier.
  output: the baseline row
  note:   A tier with no accepted baseline returns research.not_found.
invalidation list:
invalidation list
  usage:  invalidation list
  does:   List append-only invalidation tombstones.
  output: one line per tombstone: invalidation_id, date, commit, removed, reason, superseded_by
  note:   The tombstone survives artifact cleanup.
inspect candles:
inspect candles
  usage:  inspect candles <data_version>
  does:   Read a dataset's candle count and coverage.
  output: data_version, name, candles, first_bar, last_bar, bytes
  note:   Inspection is read-only and re-reads the stored bytes.
inspect timeframes:
inspect timeframes
  usage:  inspect timeframes <data_version>
  does:   Read a dataset's complete bars and partial buckets per timeframe.
  output: one line per timeframe: code, bars, partial_buckets, first_bar, last_bar
  note:   The ladder is built by the data service and cached by content.
inspect events:
inspect events
  usage:  inspect events <data_version> --timeframe <tf>
  does:   Read a dataset's event batch for one timeframe.
  output: one JSON event record per line, in the gateway's availability order
  note:   Event records carry numbers and codes; the shell does not relabel them.
verify:
verify
  usage:  verify <run_id>
  does:   Print the canonical digest the gateway recorded for a completed run.
  output: run_id and digest
  note:   The gateway computes the digest over the data artifacts; the shell never recomputes it.
  note:   A run without a digest is refused rather than printed as zero.
profile list:
profile list
  usage:  profile list
  does:   List the profiles the gateway knows, with their record counts.
  output: the active profile and one line per profile: id, name, datasets, runs, simulations
  note:   The active profile is the local default unless --profile names another.
profile create:
profile create
  usage:  profile create <name> [--id <profile_id>]
  does:   Create a profile, or return the existing one.
  output: profile_id, name, datasets, runs, simulations
  note:   Without --id the id is a slug of the name: lowercase, digits, and hyphens.
  note:   The command does not change the local default; profile use does.
profile use:
profile use
  usage:  profile use <profile_id>
  does:   Store the local default profile after the gateway confirms it exists.
  output: the active profile
  note:   An unknown profile is refused with profile.not_found and is not stored.
  note:   An explicit --profile is never written to the local default.
simulation list:
simulation list
  usage:  simulation list [--status <status>] [--limit <n>]
  does:   List the research-plane simulation runs in the active profile.
  output: one line per simulation: sim_id, status, windows, marks, premise
  note:   --status accepts draft, marking, reviewed, checked, or decided.
simulation create:
simulation create
  usage:  simulation create --premise <text> --bundle <digest> [--inputs <text>] --seed <n> --criteria <text>
  does:   Create a simulation run over a recorded model bundle.
  output: the server-assigned sim_id
  note:   The bundle is a simulation-<timeframe>.json digest from a model stage artifact.
  note:   The default window is 400 bars; a shorter bundle selects no windows.
  note:   The premise and criteria are recorded before the first mark.
  note:   Both clients send the context inputs; the same text produces the same inputs digest.
simulation windows:
simulation windows
  usage:  simulation windows <sim_id>
  does:   Select the simulation windows deterministically from its seed.
  output: the window selection the gateway returns
  note:   The gateway owns the selection; the shell prints it unchanged.
simulation mark:
simulation mark
  usage:  simulation mark <sim_id> --chart <chart> --bar <n> --action entry|exit --quality good|bad|neutral --side long|short [--note <text>]
  does:   Add one human mark to a simulation window.
  output: the server-assigned mark identity
  note:   The server assigns marked_time_utc and the mark id.
  note:   A bar outside the window is refused with simulation.mark_invalid.
simulation marks:
simulation marks
  usage:  simulation marks <sim_id> [--origin human|oracle]
  does:   List a simulation's human and oracle marks.
  output: one JSON mark record per line
  note:   Omit --origin to read every mark.
simulation oracle:
simulation oracle
  usage:  simulation oracle <sim_id>
  does:   Ask the gateway for the deterministic oracle marks.
  output: one JSON mark record per line
  note:   The oracle is synchronous and idempotent for the same inputs digest.
simulation check:
simulation check
  usage:  simulation check <sim_id>
  does:   Run the event study over the unmarked window.
  output: the check table and verdict
  note:   Fewer than 30 events, or an unmarked window, is simulation.check_incomplete.
simulation decide:
simulation decide
  usage:  simulation decide <sim_id> <test|refine|stop> [--note <text>]
  does:   Record the research decision and close marking.
  output: the decision record
  note:   Marking after a decision is refused with simulation.locked.
history list:
history list
  usage:  history list --kind <run|stage|research|simulation|dataset> [--include-archived] [--limit <n>]
  does:   List one runtime-history kind in the active profile.
  output: one header and one deterministic line per record, including its archived state
  note:   Stage runs have no archive state.
  note:   A dataset list is capped client-side when --limit is given.
history archive:
history archive
  usage:  history archive --kind <run|research|simulation|dataset> --id <id> [--dry-run]
  does:   Archive one runtime record without deleting its bytes.
  output: archived <kind> <id>
  note:   A stage has no archive; use history erase.
  note:   --dry-run prints the intent and calls nothing.
history erase:
history erase
  usage:  history erase --kind <run|stage|research|simulation|dataset> --id <id> --confirm <id> [--dry-run]
  does:   Erase one archived runtime record after typed confirmation.
  output: erased <kind> <id> bytes=<n>
  note:   --confirm must equal --id.
  note:   Succeeded runs, decided research records, checked or decided simulation runs, and referenced datasets refuse erase.
  note:   A stage erase uses the existing stage delete path.
help:
help
  usage:  help [<command>|all|glossary|workflows]
  does:   Print the command map, one command contract, or a reference topic.
  output: plain text
  note:   help all prints every contract; help glossary and help workflows print static topics.
